title: Rollout policy guardrails for Hosted canary rollouts (max step, soak, approvals, auto-stop/rollback)
creator: Paula Mendes
description:
Problem
Hosted canary rollouts are moving to GA. We need clear, enforceable policy guardrails to prevent unsafe traffic shifts and to meet enterprise governance requirements (approvals + auditability), while keeping the workflow usable for self-serve customers.

This ticket defines the GA-required guardrails and how they map to tenant entitlements and admin roles. Engineering implementation will be in policy engine + orchestrator + Console enforcement.

Scope (GA)
1) Step/traffic guardrails (percentage rollouts)
- Guardrail: max step size (max % increase of canary traffic per step)
  - Definition: max_delta_percent = new_canary_percent - current_canary_percent
  - Applies to: start rollout (0% -> initial%), step forward, manual edits to schedule (if supported)
  - Default: 25% delta (e.g., 0->25 allowed, 25->60 denied)
  - Override: enterprise policy can set smaller/larger values (hard cap TBD)

- Guardrail: minimum soak time between step changes
  - Definition: time since last step change must be >= min_soak_minutes
  - Default: 30 minutes
  - Notes: soak is measured from “step becomes active in routing” timestamp, not when user clicks “Next step”.

- Guardrail: rollout schedule must end at 100% or be explicitly stopped/rolled back
  - For GA, allow “hold at X% indefinitely” only if user explicitly pauses AND confirms (copy per DES-742). Otherwise we’ve seen teams forget rollouts mid-flight.

2) Approval gates (RBAC + thresholds)
- Requirement: approval gate is policy-configurable, but we need a strong default for enterprise tiers.

Proposed approval model
- Actions that may require approval:
  - Start rollout
  - Increase canary percent above approval_threshold_percent (e.g., >25%)
  - Rollback (optional; default no approval needed)
  - Resume after auto-stop/pause (approval required if continuing above threshold)

- Default thresholds by plan/tier (proposed; confirm with GTM/pricing)
  - Self-serve (no enterprise governance add-on): no approvals required; guardrails still enforced.
  - Enterprise Governance add-on (flag): approvals required for:
    - Start rollout if initial canary > 10%
    - Any step that increases canary above 25%

Roles & permissions (customer visible)
- Existing roles: Owner / Admin / Developer / Viewer (names may differ per tenant; map to internal RBAC).
- Add a new role capability: rollout_approver
  - Permissions: approve_rollout_action, view_rollout_policy_denials
  - Note: approver can be a subset of Admins.

Mapping to internal RBAC bundle
- Align with: sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311-rollout-approver-role-and-permissions.json
- Console should surface who can approve and how to request approval.

Auditability requirements
- All denied actions must return a policy reason string suitable for customer display (no internal-only jargon).
- All approved actions must emit audit events with:
  - actor, action, rollout_id, route_id, baseline_version, canary_version
  - before/after traffic split
  - policy snapshot hash/id (to prove which policy was in effect)
  - approval chain: requested_by, approved_by, approved_at (if applicable)

3) Auto-stop / auto-rollback policy
Goal: provide safe defaults that prevent widespread incidents, without creating alert storms or constant pauses for noisy endpoints.

Required stop conditions (GA)
- 5xx error rate regression (baseline vs canary) OR absolute 5xx error rate
- timeout rate regression OR absolute timeout rate
- p95 latency regression (relative) AND absolute p95 latency threshold

Proposed default behavior (Hosted)
- Auto-stop (pause rollout) is the default action.
- Auto-rollback is available but gated behind explicit enablement in the wizard (checkbox) and enterprise entitlement. Rationale: rollback may not be safe if canary is fixing a bug; some customers prefer pause + inspect.

Suggested defaults (beta-derived; final values owned by SRE)
- Evaluate over a rolling window: 5 minutes, require 2 consecutive failures to trigger (mitigates spikes)
- 5xx:
  - Absolute: > 1.0% OR
  - Regression: canary_5xx > baseline_5xx + 0.5% (absolute percentage points)
- Timeouts:
  - Absolute: > 0.5% OR
  - Regression: canary_timeouts > baseline_timeouts + 0.25%
- p95 latency:
  - Absolute: canary_p95 > 2.5s AND
  - Regression: canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.25

Policy tunability
- Customers can set stop condition thresholds per rollout (within admin-defined bounds) OR be locked to org defaults.
- For GA, we support per-rollout threshold overrides in Console only if tenant has enterprise entitlement; otherwise defaults apply.

Non-goals (GA)
- Automated quality gates based on evals (allow manual checklists / external links only).
- Multi-armed bandit or dynamic traffic shaping.
- Dedicated/Private parity (but schema must not paint us into a corner).

UX requirements (Console)
- Wizard must show:
  - max step + min soak constraints up-front (and validate schedule)
  - which actions require approval, and from whom
  - what will happen on SLO breach (pause vs rollback)
- Error states should be actionable:
  - “This step increases canary from 25% to 60%, which exceeds your org’s max step increase of 25%. Choose a smaller step or request a policy change from an admin.”

Open questions
1) How do we scope the Enterprise Governance add-on entitlement name/flag? (Need alignment with packaging.)
2) Do we require approval for rollback? (Default: no, to reduce MTTR; Security has asked for optional approval.)
3) Are policy defaults global or per-region? (Assumption: policy is global; metrics evaluation is per-region + global rollup.)
4) How do we treat “decrease canary percent”? (Assumption: always allowed, never requires approval; still audited.)

Acceptance criteria
- Policy schema supports: max_step_delta_percent, min_soak_minutes, approval_threshold_percent, require_approval_on_start (bool), allow_auto_rollback (entitlement-gated), stop_conditions config (thresholds + evaluation settings).
- Policy engine denies invalid actions with clear reasons; Console displays reason.
- Approval flow is enforceable (cannot bypass via API) and audited.
- Auto-stop triggers pause and emits event; optional auto-rollback triggers rollback and emits event.
- GA defaults documented in PRD + docs.

comments: 2025-02-12 (Paula Mendes): Creating this as the source of truth for GA guardrails. Please keep implementation details in ENG tickets, but decisions/defaults here so Docs + Support have something stable to reference.

2025-02-13 (Sean Gallagher): Strong preference for auto-stop default (pause) vs auto-rollback. Rollback can amplify issues if the baseline is already hot. Also +1 to requiring 2 consecutive windows before triggering to reduce noise.

2025-02-14 (Marcus Lin): Need explicit mapping to roles. For enterprise customers, approvals + audit logs are the governance story. Also, audit event should include policy_version or hash; otherwise we can’t prove which guardrails were enforced at the time.

2025-02-17 (Dylan Brooks): Wizard validations should use the same policy eval as API (don’t duplicate logic). We should add a “Preview plan” endpoint that returns: allowed/denied + required_approvals + computed schedule with soak times. (Tracking in ENG-9140 / PR-28863.)

2025-02-19 (Jordan Lee): Policy precedence: for a denied action we’ll return a structured reason internally, but Console needs a single customer-facing string. Suggest we standardize reason codes + templated messages. Will implement reason codes in ENG-9146, but PM should provide copy guidelines.
2025-02-25 (Paula Mendes): Updated defaults based on SRE feedback. Still pending final numbers after beta data review. Added note that soak time starts when routing is active (not click time).

2025-03-03 (Rafael Mendes): On-call note: please ensure auto-stop emits a paging-friendly notification and includes a link to cohort dashboard + rollout timeline. Otherwise we’ll burn time collecting context. (Wiring in ENG-9158 + dashboards in ENG-9152/PR-28910.)
2025-03-07 (Paula Mendes): Added entitlement gating proposal (Enterprise Governance add-on). Need Soojin + Marissa to confirm packaging name so docs don’t drift.

2025-03-12 (Kevin Osei): Audit retention/export: we should clarify that rollout audit events follow standard audit retention policy, and enterprise can export to SIEM. Please add to docs (Wei/Elliot).

2025-03-18 (Paula Mendes): Open question #2 (rollback approval) — tentative decision: rollback never requires approval by default; enterprise may opt into requiring approval for manual rollback, but auto-rollback must not require approval (otherwise it defeats safety). Waiting on Security sign-off.
